44. Section] The Superintendent of Courtesans 125

A courtesan who refuses to visit a man by order of the King shall be fined one thousand <term>paṇas</term> <gloss>units of currency</gloss>, or five thousand.

If she accepts the fee but acts with hostility, she shall pay a fine double the fee.

If she misappropriates the fee upon receiving it, she shall pay back eight times the amount, except in cases involving the man's illness or misconduct.

If she subjects a man to distress, she shall be cast into water <note>a form of ordeal or punishment</note>.

The fine for anyone who steals the ornaments or the fee of a courtesan is eight times the value.

The courtesan must report her fees, future income, and the man <note>who is her patron</note>.

By this same rule, actors, dancers, singers, musicians, those who make a living from art, stage performers, acrobats, and wandering bards who are accompanied by women, as well as those who live by disguise, are regulated.

They shall pay five <term>paṇas</term> as a fee for the performance if it is a traveling troupe.

Those who live by beauty <term>rūpājīvā</term> <gloss>courtesans</gloss> shall pay double the fee for a month.

A courtesan shall cause her female slaves and those who live by performing on stage to learn singing, playing instruments, reading, dancing, acting, writing, painting, playing the <term>vīṇā</term> <gloss>lute</gloss>, the flute, and the <term>mṛdaṅga</term> <gloss>drum</gloss>, as well as knowledge of the moods of others, the use of perfumes and garlands, how to enchant, prepare substances, massage, and the arts of gallantry. They shall earn their living through the royal circle. They shall make the sons of courtesans and those who live by the stage into leaders. This also applies to all musical performances.

Women who are skilled in secret codes and foreign languages should be employed to oversee those who are not trustworthy, in order to prevent espionage, assassination, or negligence, using their relatives and vehicles.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, the Superintendent of Courtesans, in the Book of the Superintendents.

Forty-eighth from the beginning.

---

<note>Notes: 1. Puruṣebhyaḥ (for men). 2. Bharaṇamarthaṃ (for ornaments). 3. Tālāpacāraṃśca (and performance techniques) is a variant reading.</note>

<summary>This page outlines the legal obligations, administrative duties, and professional requirements for courtesans and performing artists under the authority of the Superintendent.</summary>
